# API Contract Checklist: Capability-Scoped Supports Requests

**Purpose**: Check the quality of the protocol and SDK contract requirements for compatibility, enum forward
compatibility, SDK parity, conformance coverage, and documentation, before implementation and in PR review

**Created**: 2026-11-08

**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit-checklist` command
based on feature context and requirements.

**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an
item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.

**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality.
It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Requirement Completeness

- [ ] CHK001 - Do the requirements name every SDK surface a plugin author or host touches: the read helper,
  the host call, the handler-error log, the mock option, and the conformance check? [Completeness, Spec §FR-004–FR-014]
- [ ] CHK002 - Is the conformance level of the new check (Basic, Standard, or Advanced) stated in the spec, or
  only in the plan? [Gap, Spec §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK003 - Does the spec say whether the resource-type convenience call gains a capability-aware form, or
  is that left out on purpose? [Gap, Spec §FR-007]
- [ ] CHK004 - Are release-note requirements stated, given that the issue's acceptance criteria list "release
  notes" and the changelog is generated from commit text? [Gap, Spec §FR-016]
- [ ] CHK005 - Does the spec say whether a plugin-side TypeScript read helper is needed for parity with
  `RequestedCapability`, or that the TS SDK is client-side only for this field? [Gap, Spec §FR-009]

## Requirement Clarity

- [ ] CHK006 - Is the "resource-scoped capability" set used by FR-014 defined in a requirement, rather than
  only in Assumptions and research? [Clarity, Spec §FR-014, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK007 - Is "answer as before the field existed" for an unspecified request specific enough that a
  reviewer can tell a conforming plugin from one that changed its default? [Clarity, Spec §FR-002]
- [ ] CHK008 - Is the mock's "not supported" answer for a listed capability specified well enough, including
  whether a reason is required and what it names? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK009 - Is the order of the mock's checks defined: is the capability considered before or after the
  provider and resource checks? [Clarity, Spec §FR-013]
- [ ] CHK010 - Does "outside the defined list" in FR-005 say explicitly whether negative values and the
  unspecified value are included? [Clarity, Spec §FR-005]

## Requirement Consistency

- [ ] CHK011 - Do FR-002 ("any capability") and the consistency edge case (a specific "supported" implies
  "supported" for unspecified) describe the same model, with the edge case stated as guidance only?
  [Consistency, Spec §FR-002, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK012 - Do FR-012 (validators accept every value) and FR-005 (the helper normalizes unknown values)
  agree on where unknown values are tolerated and where they are reinterpreted? [Consistency, Spec §FR-005, §FR-012]
- [ ] CHK013 - Do US3's acceptance scenario 3 and FR-014 agree on which capabilities a plugin that declares
  only non-resource-scoped capabilities is asked about? [Consistency, Spec §US3, §FR-014]

## Backward & Forward Compatibility

- [ ] CHK014 - Is every host and plugin version pairing (old/new host × old/new plugin, including a value newer
  than the plugin's SDK) covered by a requirement or an edge case? [Coverage, Spec §Edge Cases, §FR-003]
- [ ] CHK015 - Is the promise that existing support handlers "behave the same" bounded? Does it cover the SDK
  default answer, registry rejection, and the handler-error mapping, which are all unchanged?
  [Clarity, Spec §FR-004, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK016 - Is the minor version classification justified in the requirements, with an explicit statement
  that no field, value, or signature is removed or renamed? [Completeness, Spec §FR-003, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK017 - Is there a requirement limiting how often the unknown-value warning is logged, so a newer host
  calling on every routing decision cannot flood plugin logs? [Gap, Spec §FR-005]

## Conformance Coverage

- [ ] CHK018 - Are the failure conditions of the new check written as requirements: an error, an invalid
  response, and a failure that names the capability? [Completeness, Spec §US3, §FR-014]
- [ ] CHK019 - Does the spec say that the check never judges answer values, and does SC-002 follow from that
  for plugins that ignore the field? [Consistency, Spec §FR-015, Assumptions]
- [ ] CHK020 - Is the check's behavior defined when capability discovery fails or is unimplemented (legacy
  plugins)? [Edge Case, Spec §FR-014]

## Documentation & Measurability

- [ ] CHK021 - Does FR-016 require the docs to tell hosts that an old plugin's answer to a capability-specific
  request is its "any" answer? [Gap, Spec §FR-016, Edge Cases]
- [ ] CHK022 - Can SC-006 ("answers in one place") be checked objectively, for example by naming the guide
  section? [Measurability, Spec §SC-006]
- [ ] CHK023 - Is the zero-allocation target in FR-006 and SC-005 scoped to the known and unspecified values,
  with the unknown-value path (which logs) exempt? [Clarity, Spec §FR-006, §SC-005]
- [ ] CHK024 - Is the requirement that every documentation example compiles scoped to both the Go and
  TypeScript snippets? [Clarity, Spec §FR-016]

## Notes

- `/speckit-implement` reads checklist state but does not change the markers.
- Items marked `[Gap]` are candidates for spec edits before or during `/speckit-analyze`.
